exercise.name: Floor T Raise

reference.title: Floor T Raise
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be read at authoring time, so the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)

exercise.bodyPart: Upper back (middle trapezius, rhomboids) and rear shoulders
exercise.mechanics: Isolation (shoulder horizontal abduction with scapular retraction, prone)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the arms lift, breathe steadily in the hold, in as they lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, 2 s hold, 1 s down

prescription.tempo: About 1 s up, 2 s hold, 1 s down
prescription.load: Body weight (light plates or dumbbells later)
prescription.progression: Longer holds, then light weights in the hands, then the incline-bench T raise

cues.text: Lie face down, forehead just off the mat, arms straight out to the sides in a T, thumbs up.
Squeeze the shoulder blades back and together and lift the straight arms off the mat.
Hold, shoulders away from the ears, neck long.
Lower the arms slowly to the mat.
Relax for a moment, then repeat.

mistakes.fix: Draw the shoulder blades down and back before lifting.
Keep the forehead near the mat; only the arms lift.

kinematics.norm: Arms out at about 90 degrees from the body (T), thumbs up (Ekstrom 2003 prone horizontal abduction)
Hands a few to about 10 cm off the mat (clinical opinion)
Shoulder blades squeeze back and together (clinical opinion)
Chest and pelvis stay on the mat (clinical opinion)
About 1 s up, 2 s hold, 1 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual 13818, Floor T Raise, video (movement reference)
Ekstrom, Donatelli & Soderberg 2003, surface electromyographic analysis of exercises for the trapezius and serratus anterior muscles (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 33(5):247-258)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Shoulder pain at the front of the joint: lower the arms a little toward the body or shorten the hold.
Neck discomfort: rest the forehead on a folded towel.
modify: Bend the elbows to 90 degrees (shorter lever).

muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Middle trapezius and rhomboids retract the shoulder blade; prone horizontal abduction with external rotation was among the best middle-trapezius exercises (Ekstrom 2003).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Middle trapezius and rhomboids retract the shoulder blade (Ekstrom 2003).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Posterior deltoid lifts the straight arm in horizontal abduction.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Posterior deltoid lifts the straight arm in horizontal abduction.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Helps hold the arm out at shoulder level.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Helps hold the arm out at shoulder level.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the upper back from rounding.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Keep the upper back from rounding.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Should stay quiet: shoulders away from the ears.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Should stay quiet: shoulders away from the ears.
